runs.name: Astec Industries, Inc.
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$39.48** (close 2026-10-12, aggregator quote printed by `tools/run.py`, flagged). Shares **23,025,367**, one class (10-Q cover at 2026-07-31, acc 0000792987-26-000044, `Screens/cover_shares.py`; 22,994,624 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30, no treasury stock, the difference July vesting); cap **$909.0M**. Sovereign **5.60%** (USD; Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-09). Filings read: the FY2025 10-K (0000792987-26-000011), the June 2026 10-Q, the DEF 14A of 2026-03-13 (0001104659-26-027745), the FY2022 10-K (0000792987-23-000015) for segments as revised, the FY2018 10-K (0000792987-19-000019), the 8-Ks of 2026-04-20 and 2026-07-30; the TerraSource 8-K of 2025-07-01 and the auditor-change 8-K of 2023 seen in the index, not read. One figure cross-checked: operating cash FY2025 $61.4M on the filed cash-flow statement, equal to the `tools/run.py` line. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7. Competitors from the rivals the 10-K names that file: Gencor, Terex (Materials Processing segment, re-segmented in 2025, flagged) and Alamo Group (Morbark; XBRL only, its 10-K not opened); some 27 named rivals flagged as not SEC filers (Fayat, Ammann, Metso, Sandvik, Epiroc and others); Caterpillar and Deere file but do not report the lines apart. **Q1 IN**: a cyclical, slow-changing steel machinery and parts business for road building whose economics can be read from its own and its rivals' filings. **Q2 OUT** on Infrastructure Solutions, which decides at 69.0% of five-year Segment Operating Adjusted EBITDA (Materials Solutions 31.0%; the shares measured on the filer's only segment profit, a CONVENTION of the run): about 3% a year on equity 2016 to 2025, equity $648M to $682M and retained earnings $537M to $568M in nine years; the filer's own words "competition limits our ability to pass through cost increases in many cases" (Item 7), gross margin 20.7% and operating margin 0.6% in the 2022 steel squeeze; larger, better-resourced named rivals inside the field; operating margin over the whole span 2.4% (2016 to 2025) against Gencor 10.0%, Alamo 9.6% (2016 to 2025) and Terex Materials Processing 14.3% (2020 to 2025); all Materials goodwill ($20.2M) written off in 2024; the 2023 to 2025 improvement weighed and not credited (best year 2025: 5.7% on equity, 9.2% pre-tax on tangible capital; first half 2026 operating margin 3.7% against 6.4%). Q3 to Q12 not reached. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash 2021 to 2025 -18.7, -121.4, -10.4, -2.5, +13.6 ($M), five-year mean -$27.9M equity-only, -$23.1M all-equity (ten-year mean +$13.2M equity-only); serial acquirer rule puts the organic pair central; the series changes sign so the range is the no-growth case alone, **-$31.55 a share** all-equity (equity-only -$21.62), net debt $314.8M at 2026-06-30, against $39.48; no case earns the floor; fair **-$23.68** all-equity, -$12.11 equity-only, no positive figure; no alert. Balance sheets 2016 to 2025: inventory 24% to 33% of sales and the swing behind owner cash +121 (2020) to -121 (2022); debt near zero 2019 to 2021, $393.4M at 2026-06-30 after TerraSource ($252.6M, 2025-07-01) and CWMF ($70.1M, 2026-01-01); goodwill and intangibles $36M to $271.7M, about two fifths of equity. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: the 2019 shareholder class action settled for $13.7M funded entirely by insurers; the 2018 material weaknesses; immaterial income-tax provision errors recorded in 2024; the Infrastructure group president left 2026-04-20. Contamination declared by the analyst: a directory listing of `Test Runs/` filtered to today's date showed thirteen other 2026-10-13 run names (none about Astec), VELO commit subjects, AYI and ARCB folder names, memory index queue lines; nothing used. Commits d7f15c94, 8db03746, 8ef3884d, 5ab4ab1f, f0bd429f. Citations: the analyst's check PASS; the dispatcher's script (`dispatcher_cite_check.py`) checked 11 quotations, its four flags line-wrap artifacts, each confirmed by hand against its row; every id in the ledger, no E-id. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q2's full-cycle deferral of a change for the better would send any improving business TOO HARD (NATURE); the analyst read it as applying only where crediting the change would decide the box, and closed OUT; the text should say which; (2) the parts rule needs a segment operating profit the filer does not report, and says nothing on central costs; (3) the "standing castle that protects only ordinary returns" item has no sentence for the weak participant in a field that earns decent returns; (4) with a range that is a point, Part VII's two-end average and the width test do not apply; (5) the after-tax interest rate for the all-equity basis is unnamed (the filer's 26.9% used, confessed). Could not get: Alamo's 10-K text and Gencor's earlier 10-Ks (XBRL transcription), Terex Materials Processing 2016 to 2019, segment depreciation, the prices paid in the 2018 and 2022 buybacks.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a road-building equipment and parts maker (asphalt and concrete plants, pavers, crushers; TerraSource bought 2025-07-01, CWMF 2026-01-01) whose castle is shown open: about 3% a year on equity 2016 to 2025 with equity flat for nine years, the filer's own words that competition limits cost pass-through, and filing rivals (Gencor 10.0%, Alamo 9.6%, Terex Materials Processing 14.3%) earning several times its 2.4% operating margin over the whole span; the 2023 to 2025 improvement weighed and not credited. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range -$31.55 a share all-equity (no-growth case alone) against $39.48, fair -$23.68 all-equity (-$12.11 equity-only), no positive figure, not armed. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: the 2019 class action settled by insurers, the 2018 material weaknesses, the 2024 tax-provision errors.
